note: Split engine. calculateIPSS(state) returns { ipssScore, ipssCategoryLabel, firedRules } — the sum of the seven IPSS items (null items are skipped entirely, with no completeness penalty), the label Mild (0-7) / Moderate (8-19) / Severe (20-35), and one fired rule IPSS-0N per item whose answer is > 0 (a 0 answer counts toward the total but fires nothing), in question order. form-app.js then calls detectAdditionalFlags(state) separately and stores it as additionalFlags, so flagsHint/flagsArgs mirror that single-argument call; the oracle stores its output under expected.additionalFlags. Quirks verified: the detector recomputes its own IPSS total treating null as 0 (same result as the grader); PSA fires only when > 4.0 (4.0 exactly is silent) and eGFR only when < 60 (60 exactly is silent); retention needs straining 'yes' AND stream exactly 'weak' ('intermittent' does not count); FLAG-NEURO-001 embeds 'details not specified' when neurologicConditionDetails is blank; flags are stable-sorted high > medium > low so within a priority they keep detection order. ipssCategoryKey/qolScore/timestamp are assembled by form-app.js, not the grader, so they are not part of expected. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas urology-assessment --update

personas.name: Moderate boundary with two IPSS items unanswered, PSA 4.0 and eGFR 60 exactly
personas.description: 58-year-old man with Parkinson's-type symptoms under investigation (neurological condition marked yes but details left blank) who skipped IPSS Q2 and Q6. Answered items 2,1,2,0,3 = total 8 -> 'Moderate' at the lower boundary; firedRules = IPSS-01 (2), IPSS-03 (1), IPSS-04 (2), IPSS-07 (3). PSA is exactly 4.0 and eGFR exactly 60, so neither threshold flag fires; straining 'yes' with an 'intermittent' stream does not meet the retention rule. Expect exactly 2 additionalFlags in priority order: FLAG-NEURO-001 (medium, message ending 'details not specified') then FLAG-ED-001 (low, ED with total >= 8).
